description: The article develops a dialogic-thematic analysis procedure, grounded in Bakhtinian concepts, for mapping meaning-making in blended collaborative settings.
title: Dialogic thematic analysis: centripetal and centrifugal forces as an analytic framework for meaning-making

description: DST holds that, as the article states, \"the self is populated by other inner selves that collectively derive from the world and have their own voice, motives, opinions, and knowledge that become present in what are known as I-positions via dialogue in response to the social situation\".
title: Dialogical self theory (DST) I-positions as a CSCL analytical framework

description: The article's second model assesses collaboration \"from a dialogical perspective\" as the participation of different speakers through their voices.
title: Dialogical voice-synergy model of collaboration

description: The DAC system identifies \"dialogue acts\", the communicative function of each utterance typed during online collaboration, building on the Verbal Observation System and discourse-analysis research.
title: Dialogue Act Coding (DAC) system

title: Difference I/E model

description: A framework representing threaded CSCL discussion as a directed post-reply network in which centrality measures operationalize the uptake of ideas and stimulation of further discussion.
title: Diffusion-based centrality framework for measuring uptake in CSCL discourse

description: The report urges researchers to use the robust log data DLPs generate, such as which tasks students begin, time spent, and detailed progress.
title: Digital learning platform process-data analysis

description: Digital shadowing is the article's organising methodological framework: unlike digital twins, shadows record system behaviour without feedback loops.
title: Digital shadowing as a framework for recording LLM behaviour under controlled conditions

description: The article identifies the DINA model and the DINO model as \"two typical theoretical diagnostic classification models\".
title: DINA and DINO cognitive diagnostic models

description: The study adapts Pomerantz's strong/weak disagreement distinction into a two-category coding scheme for dissenting turns in peer critique.
title: Direct and soft disagreement taxonomy for coding peer critique talk

description: The article supplies the theoretical basis for using its discrimination index as the foundation of a Q-matrix validation method.
title: Discrimination-index Q-matrix validation for cognitive diagnostic models

title: Distributional treatment effects framework

description: The editorial describes Tissenbaum, Berland, and Lyons' framework \"for recognizing and coding collaboration and divergent learning — Divergent Collaborative Learning Mechanisms (DCLM)\", used to analyze museum visitors' interactions with an interactive digital tabletop exhibit.
title: Divergent Collaborative Learning Mechanisms (DCLM) framework
